name: Sharing readiness (this PC)
purpose: Network profile (Public hides everything), the services discovery and sharing need, the File and Printer Sharing firewall rules, and the SMB client settings that block guest shares
note: Read-only, no admin. Says separately whether this PC can reach others and whether others can reach it.

run.display: network profile → sharing services → firewall rules → SMB client settings
run.command:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
# 1. the network profile of every connected adapter - Windows hides this PC and refuses sharing on Public
# A VPN or overlay adapter (WireGuard, Tailscale, OpenVPN...) is normally Public and that does not affect sharing on the LAN adapter
$vpnRx = 'VPN|WireGuard|Tailscale|NetBird|OpenVPN|TAP-Windows|Wintun|ZeroTier|Cisco AnyConnect|Fortinet|GlobalProtect|Mullvad|NordLynx|Proton|ExpressVPN|Surfshark|WAN Miniport \((PPTP|L2TP|SSTP|IKEv2)\)'
$vpnAliases = @(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.InterfaceDescription -match $vpnRx -or $_.Name -match 'VPN|^wt\d|tailscale|^zt|Mullvad|Proton|Nord' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Name })
$profiles = @(Get-NetConnectionProfile | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Adapter = $_.InterfaceAlias; Network = $_.Name; Profile = [string]$_.NetworkCategory; Internet = [string]$_.IPv4Connectivity; Kind = (& { if ($vpnAliases -contains $_.InterfaceAlias) { 'VPN' } else { 'LAN' } }) } })
'1. Network profile (discovery and sharing are off on Public networks)'
if ($profiles.Count) { ($profiles | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 4096).TrimEnd() } else { '   No connected network.' }
$public = @($profiles | Where-Object { $_.Profile -eq 'Public' -and $_.Kind -eq 'LAN' })
$vpnPublic = @($profiles | Where-Object { $_.Profile -eq 'Public' -and $_.Kind -eq 'VPN' })
if ($vpnPublic.Count) { '   (' + (($vpnPublic | ForEach-Object { $_.Adapter }) -join ', ') + ' is a VPN adapter on the Public profile - normal, and it does not affect sharing on your LAN adapter.)' }
$active = @($profiles | Where-Object { $_.Kind -eq 'LAN' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Profile -replace 'DomainAuthenticated', 'Domain' } | Sort-Object -Unique)
''
# 2. the services that discovery and sharing depend on
$svcNames = @(@('LanmanWorkstation', 'Workstation (reaches other PCs'' shares)'), @('LanmanServer', 'Server (offers this PC''s shares)'), @('FDResPub', 'Function Discovery Resource Publication (makes this PC visible)'), @('fdPHost', 'Function Discovery Provider Host (finds other devices)'), @('SSDPSRV', 'SSDP Discovery'), @('upnphost', 'UPnP Device Host'), @('Dnscache', 'DNS Client (also answers .local and NetBIOS names)'))
$svcRows = @(foreach ($s in $svcNames) { $svc = Get-Service -Name $s[0]; [pscustomobject]@{ Service = $s[1]; Status = (& { if ($svc) { [string]$svc.Status } else { 'not present' } }); 'Start type' = (& { if ($svc) { [string]$svc.StartType } else { '' } }) } })
'2. Discovery and sharing services'
($svcRows | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 4096).TrimEnd()
# Workstation and DNS Client are needed to reach anything; Server and FDResPub only to be reached; fdPHost/SSDP/UPnP start on demand
$stopped = @($svcRows | Where-Object { $_.Status -ne 'Running' -and $_.Service -match '^(Workstation|DNS Client)' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Service })
$notVisible = @($svcRows | Where-Object { $_.Status -ne 'Running' -and $_.Service -match '^(Server|Function Discovery Resource)' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Service })
''
# 3. the firewall rules that let other PCs in
$fw = @(Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup 'File and Printer Sharing' -Direction Inbound | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -match 'SMB-In|NB-Session-In|ICMPv4-In' } | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Rule = $_.DisplayName; Enabled = [string]$_.Enabled; Profile = [string]$_.Profile } })
'3. Firewall rules for sharing (inbound)'
if ($fw.Count) { ($fw | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 4096).TrimEnd() } else { '   The "File and Printer Sharing" rule group was not found.' }
$smbInActive = @($fw | Where-Object { $_.Rule -match 'SMB-In' -and $_.Enabled -eq 'True' } | Where-Object { $rule = $_; @($active | Where-Object { $rule.Profile -eq 'Any' -or $rule.Profile -match $_ }).Count -gt 0 })
''
# 4. SMB client settings that quietly block NAS boxes and old devices
$cli = Get-SmbClientConfiguration
$guest = (& { if ($cli) { [bool]$cli.EnableInsecureGuestLogons } else { $false } })
'4. SMB client on this PC'
if ($cli) { '   Guest (no-password) shares: ' + (& { if ($guest) { 'allowed' } else { 'BLOCKED - the Windows default since 2017. A NAS or old device share that needs no password fails with "You can''t access this shared folder"; give the share a user and password, or allow insecure guest logons in Group Policy.' } }); '   SMB signing required: ' + [string]$cli.RequireSecuritySignature } else { '   Could not read the SMB client configuration.' }
''
'5. This PC''s side of it'
if ($public.Count) { 'PROBLEM: ' + (($public | ForEach-Object { $_.Adapter }) -join ', ') + ' is set to Public. On a Public network Windows neither looks for other devices nor lets them in. Fix: Settings > Network & internet > (your connection) > Network profile type > Private.' }
elseif ($stopped.Count) { 'PROBLEM: not running - ' + ($stopped -join '; ') + '. Nothing on the network can be reached by name without it (services.msc: set to Automatic and start it).' }
else { 'Reaching other PCs: ready (' + ($active -join '/') + ' profile, Workstation and DNS Client running).' }
$seen = @(); if ($notVisible.Count) { $seen += ($notVisible -join '; ') + ' not running' }; if (-not $smbInActive.Count) { $seen += 'no inbound SMB firewall rule enabled for the ' + ($active -join '/') + ' profile' }
if ($seen.Count) { 'Being reached by others: NOT possible - ' + ($seen -join '; ') + '. Only matters if other PCs should open shares on this PC (Settings > Network & internet > Advanced sharing settings > File and printer sharing: On).' } else { 'Being reached by others: ready (Server service up, SMB allowed in).' }
'SUMMARY ' + ([pscustomobject]@{ profiles = $profiles; public = ($public.Count -gt 0); publicAdapters = @($public | ForEach-Object { $_.Adapter }); stopped = $stopped; notVisible = $notVisible; smbIn = ($smbInActive.Count -gt 0); guest = $guest; active = ($active -join ',') } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 3)

name: Remote Desktop host status
purpose: Whether this PC can accept Remote Desktop: edition, the enabled setting, the service, the listening port, the firewall rules for the current network profile, and who may connect
note: Read-only registry and service reads; no admin needed to look. Changing any of it needs an administrator.
win: registry (Terminal Server) + Get-Service TermService + Get-NetTCPConnection + Get-NetFirewallRule (Remote Desktop)

run.display: edition → enabled → service → listening → firewall → users
run.command:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
$os = Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem
$edition = [string]$os.Caption
$isHome = [bool]($edition -match ' Home')   # ($home is PowerShell's own variable for the profile folder)
$ts = Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server'
$deny = -1; if ($ts -and $null -ne $ts.fDenyTSConnections) { $deny = [int]$ts.fDenyTSConnections }
$tcp = Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp'
$nla = -1; if ($tcp -and $null -ne $tcp.UserAuthentication) { $nla = [int]$tcp.UserAuthentication }
$port = 3389; if ($tcp -and $tcp.PortNumber) { $port = [int]$tcp.PortNumber }
$svc = Get-Service -Name TermService
$listen = @(Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen -LocalPort $port)
$fw = @(Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup 'Remote Desktop' -Direction Inbound | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Rule = $_.DisplayName; Enabled = [string]$_.Enabled; Profile = [string]$_.Profile } })
$profiles = @(Get-NetConnectionProfile | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Adapter = $_.InterfaceAlias; Profile = [string]$_.NetworkCategory } })
$active = @($profiles | ForEach-Object { $_.Profile -replace 'DomainAuthenticated', 'Domain' } | Sort-Object -Unique)
$fwOk = @($fw | Where-Object { $_.Enabled -eq 'True' -and $_.Rule -match 'TCP-In' } | Where-Object { $rule = $_; @($active | Where-Object { $rule.Profile -eq 'Any' -or $rule.Profile -match $_ }).Count -gt 0 })
$members = @(net localgroup "Remote Desktop Users" 2>$null | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch '^(Alias name|Comment|Members|-+$|The command completed)' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() })
$me = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
$adminGroup = [bool](($me.Groups | ForEach-Object { $_.Value }) -contains 'S-1-5-32-544')
$ips = @(Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notlike '169.254.*' -and $_.IPAddress -ne '127.0.0.1' } | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.IPAddress })
'1. Windows edition: ' + $edition + (& { if ($isHome) { '   -> Home editions cannot HOST Remote Desktop (they can connect out, not accept connections)' } else { '' } })
'2. Remote Desktop enabled: ' + (& { if ($deny -eq 0) { 'yes' } elseif ($deny -eq 1) { 'NO   (Settings > System > Remote Desktop > On)' } else { 'unknown' } }) + '   Network Level Authentication required: ' + (& { if ($nla -eq 1) { 'yes' } elseif ($nla -eq 0) { 'no' } else { 'unknown' } }) + '   Port: ' + $port + (& { if ($port -ne 3389) { ' (non-standard: connect to ' + $env:COMPUTERNAME + ':' + $port + ')' } else { '' } })
'3. Remote Desktop Services (TermService): ' + (& { if ($svc) { [string]$svc.Status + ' (' + [string]$svc.StartType + ')' } else { 'not found' } })
'4. Listening on TCP ' + $port + ': ' + (& { if ($listen.Count) { 'yes (' + (@($listen | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.LocalAddress } | Sort-Object -Unique) -join ', ') + ')' } else { 'NO' } })
'5. Firewall rules (Remote Desktop group, inbound):'
if ($fw.Count) { ($fw | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 4096).TrimEnd() } else { '   none found' }
'   Active network profile: ' + ($active -join ', ') + '   -> ' + (& { if ($fwOk.Count) { 'an enabled Remote Desktop rule covers it' } else { 'NO enabled Remote Desktop rule covers it' } })
'6. Who may connect: members of Administrators' + (& { if ($members.Count) { ', plus Remote Desktop Users: ' + ($members -join ', ') } else { ' (the Remote Desktop Users group is empty)' } }) + '.  You are ' + (& { if ($adminGroup) { 'an administrator' } else { 'NOT an administrator' } }) + '.'
'7. This PC: ' + $env:COMPUTERNAME + ' at ' + ($ips -join ', ')
'SUMMARY ' + ([pscustomobject]@{ edition = $edition; home = $isHome; enabled = ($deny -eq 0); enabledKnown = ($deny -ne -1); nla = ($nla -eq 1); port = $port; service = (& { if ($svc) { [string]$svc.Status } else { '' } }); listening = ($listen.Count -gt 0); fwRule = ($fwOk.Count -gt 0); profiles = ($active -join ','); rdpUsers = $members; admin = $adminGroup; computer = $env:COMPUTERNAME; ips = $ips } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 3)

name: Local network scan
purpose: Find every device on your own network: pings all addresses in your subnet at once, then adds MAC addresses and names
note: Scans only the private subnet this PC is on (at most 254 addresses). There is nothing to type, and it refuses to run on a public address.
win: Ping sweep of your local subnet (PowerShell)

run.display: Ping sweep of your local subnet + ARP table
run.command: $ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'; $sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew(); $routes = @(Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' | Sort-Object RouteMetric, InterfaceMetric); $me = $null; $gw = $null; foreach ($r in $routes) { $a = @(Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceIndex $r.InterfaceIndex -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notlike '169.254.*' -and $_.AddressState -eq 'Preferred' }); if ($a.Count) { $me = $a[0]; $gw = $r.NextHop; break } }; if (-not $me) { 'SCAN-ERROR: no active network adapter with an IPv4 address was found.'; exit 1 }; $o = @($me.IPAddress.Split('.') | ForEach-Object { [int]$_ }); $private = ($o[0] -eq 10) -or ($o[0] -eq 192 -and $o[1] -eq 168) -or ($o[0] -eq 172 -and $o[1] -ge 16 -and $o[1] -le 31); if (-not $private) { 'SCAN-ERROR: this adapter has a public address (' + $me.IPAddress + '). NetDeck only scans private local networks.'; exit 1 }; $prefix = [int]$me.PrefixLength; if ($prefix -lt 24) { $prefix = 24 }; $size = [int][math]::Pow(2, 32 - $prefix); $start = [int]([math]::Floor($o[3] / $size) * $size); $first = $start + 1; $last = $start + $size - 2; if ($last -lt $first) { 'SCAN-ERROR: this subnet is too small to scan.'; exit 1 }; $base = [string]$o[0] + '.' + $o[1] + '.' + $o[2] + '.'; $targets = @($first..$last | ForEach-Object { $base + $_ }); $jobs = foreach ($t in $targets) { $p = New-Object System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping; [pscustomobject]@{ IP = $t; Task = $p.SendPingAsync($t, 1000) } }; try { [void][System.Threading.Tasks.Task]::WaitAll([System.Threading.Tasks.Task[]]@($jobs | ForEach-Object { $_.Task }), 8000) } catch { }; $alive = @{}; foreach ($j in $jobs) { if ($j.Task.Status -eq 'RanToCompletion' -and $j.Task.Result.Status -eq 'Success') { $alive[$j.IP] = $j.Task.Result.RoundtripTime } }; $macs = @{}; Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 -InterfaceIndex $me.InterfaceIndex | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'Unreachable' -and $_.State -ne 'Incomplete' -and $_.LinkLayerAddress -and $_.LinkLayerAddress -notmatch '^(FF-FF|00-00-00-00|01-00-5E)' } | ForEach-Object { $macs[$_.IPAddress] = $_.LinkLayerAddress }; $myMac = (Get-NetAdapter -InterfaceIndex $me.InterfaceIndex).MacAddress; $found = @($targets | Where-Object { $alive.ContainsKey($_) -or $macs.ContainsKey($_) }); if (-not ($found -contains $me.IPAddress)) { $found += $me.IPAddress }; $look = foreach ($f in $found) { [pscustomobject]@{ IP = $f; Task = [System.Net.Dns]::GetHostEntryAsync($f) } }; try { [void][System.Threading.Tasks.Task]::WaitAll([System.Threading.Tasks.Task[]]@($look | ForEach-Object { $_.Task }), 4000) } catch { }; $names = @{}; foreach ($l in $look) { if ($l.Task.Status -eq 'RanToCompletion') { $n = $l.Task.Result.HostName; if ($n -and $n -ne $l.IP -and $n -notmatch 'docker\.internal$') { $names[$l.IP] = $n } } }; $rows = @(foreach ($f in ($found | Sort-Object { [int]($_.Split('.')[3]) })) { $note = ''; if ($f -eq $me.IPAddress) { $note = 'this PC' } elseif ($f -eq $gw) { $note = 'router' }; $mac = [string]$macs[$f]; if ($f -eq $me.IPAddress) { $mac = [string]$myMac }; $ping = 'no reply'; if ($alive.ContainsKey($f)) { $ping = 'replied' }; [pscustomobject]@{ IP = $f; Name = [string]$names[$f]; MAC = $mac; Ping = $ping; Note = $note } }); 'Scanned ' + $base + $first + '-' + $last + ' on ' + $me.InterfaceAlias + ' in ' + [math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, 1) + ' s: ' + $rows.Count + ' devices found'; $rows | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 4096

name: Discover announcing devices
purpose: Asks the network who is there over mDNS/Bonjour and SSDP/UPnP: TVs, speakers, printers, Apple and Google devices answer with their own names and models
note: Listens for about 4 seconds. Only devices that announce themselves appear; the network scan finds the rest. Names it learns are remembered for a week and shown in the scan table.

run.display: SSDP M-SEARCH + mDNS PTR queries for ~30 service types, 4 s listen, UPnP descriptions fetched

name: Device port probe
purpose: "What is this thing?" — tests 26 common device ports on one address at once (web, printing, casting, file sharing, cameras, remote access) and says what it looks like
note: One TCP connection attempt per port, 2.5 s in total. Only probe devices on networks you are responsible for. The scan table has a "probe" button on every row.

run.display: TCP connect {host} on 26 common ports (2.5 s)

name: Router check-up
purpose: Your router from the inside: management ports (telnet!), admin page and certificate, and whether UPnP is on and what ports it has opened to the internet
note: Talks only to your default gateway on a private address. Read-only: it lists UPnP port forwards, it never adds or removes any.
win: TCP probes of management ports + admin page fetch + UPnP IGD GetGenericPortMappingEntry

run.display: gateway → port probe → admin page/TLS → UPnP forwards → verdict

name: Router WAN address (UPnP)
purpose: Asks your router, over UPnP, what address it has on its internet side. A private address there means a second router in front of it (double NAT); a 100.64.x address means carrier-grade NAT
note: Only your own gateway on a private address; one read-only UPnP request (GetExternalIPAddress). Routers with UPnP off cannot be asked.

run.display: gateway → UPnP discovery → GetExternalIPAddress

name: nmap
purpose: Port and host scanning
note: Usually not installed, and only for hosts you're authorized to scan.

name: pktmon / tcpdump
purpose: Packet capture
note: Captures traffic and needs admin rights — run it yourself.

name: Packet capture (timed)
purpose: Record this PC's own traffic for a few seconds, then summarise it: protocols, who it talked to, DNS names looked up
note: Needs administrator rights — use "Run as admin" first. Records only what this PC sends and receives, keeps the first 256 bytes of each packet, and deletes the recording afterwards unless you pick the keep variant; the decoded text stays for the Capture viewer.
win: pktmon start --capture --comp nics; pktmon stop; pktmon etl2txt

run.display: pktmon start --capture (10 s) → stop → etl2txt → summary

presets.label: 30 seconds
presets.display: pktmon start --capture (30 s) → stop → etl2txt → summary

presets.label: 60 seconds
presets.display: pktmon start --capture (60 s) → stop → etl2txt → summary

presets.label: 30 seconds, keep a .pcapng on the Desktop for Wireshark
presets.display: pktmon start --capture (30 s) → stop → etl2txt → summary + etl2pcap

name: Packet capture (filtered)
purpose: The timed capture narrowed to one thing — DNS only, one host, one port, or ARP/broadcast — so the summary shows just that conversation
note: Needs administrator rights — use "Run as admin" first. Same limits as the timed capture: this PC's own traffic, first 256 bytes of each packet, recording deleted afterwards (the decoded text stays for the Capture viewer). Only capture traffic you are entitled to see.
win: pktmon filter add …; pktmon start --capture (20 s); pktmon stop; pktmon etl2txt
unix: sudo tcpdump -i any arp or broadcast

run.display: pktmon filter -p 53 → capture 20 s → summary

presets.label: one host — everything to or from an address
one port — TCP or UDP
ARP & broadcast only — who is asking for whom
presets.display: pktmon filter -d ARP / broadcast → capture 20 s → summary

name: Packet counters (live)
purpose: Packets in, out and dropped per second on every adapter — and which driver layer (firewall, VPN, filter) is dropping them
note: Needs administrator rights — use "Run as admin" first. Counts only; nothing is recorded. Run it while the problem is happening (a stalled download, a failing ping) to see where packets disappear.
win: pktmon start --capture --counters-only; pktmon counters; pktmon stop

run.display: pktmon start --capture --counters-only → pktmon counters --json every second for 10 s → stop

presets.label: 30 seconds
presets.display: pktmon start --capture --counters-only → pktmon counters --json every second for 30 s → stop

presets.label: 60 seconds
presets.display: pktmon start --capture --counters-only → pktmon counters --json every second for 60 s → stop

name: Capture viewer
purpose: The last packet capture as a table — time, source, destination, protocol, size, decode — with variants for DNS only and connection attempts only
note: Shows the most recent capture made by either capture command (kept as decoded text until the next capture). No admin needed to view. Press "Table" to sort and filter it.

run.display: decode last capture → first 1,000 packets

connection attempts only (TCP SYN) — who tried to talk to whom
presets.display: decode last capture → TCP SYN packets

name: Packet-drop hunt
purpose: Counts packets on every layer for 10 s while pinging the router and the internet and downloading 5 MB — used by the "Are packets being dropped on this PC?" playbook
win: pktmon start --capture --counters-only; ping + download; pktmon counters; pktmon stop

name: TLS certificate check
purpose: Show who issued a site's certificate, when it expires, and whether Windows trusts it

run.display: TLS certificate of {host}:443
run.command: $h = '{host}'; $c = New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient; $c.Connect($h, 443); $s = New-Object Net.Security.SslStream($c.GetStream(), $false, { $true }); $s.AuthenticateAsClient($h); $x = New-Object Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2($s.RemoteCertificate); [pscustomobject]@{ Subject = $x.Subject; Issuer = $x.Issuer; ValidFrom = $x.NotBefore.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'); ValidTo = $x.NotAfter.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'); DaysLeft = [int]($x.NotAfter - (Get-Date)).TotalDays; Protocol = $s.SslProtocol; TrustedByWindows = $x.Verify() } | Format-List; $c.Close()

note: Runs iperf3 if it is installed (put iperf3.exe in a folder on your PATH; Windows builds at github.com/ar51an/iperf3-win-builds). The other machine runs "iperf3 -s". Windows Firewall will ask once when this PC acts as the server.
